newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH STEEL-MAKERS WANT LONGER MARKET PROTECTION.
newsitem.headline: POLISH STEEL-MAKERS WANT LONGER MARKET PROTECTION.

text.p: Polish steel-makers want the government to postpone the abolition of duties on imported steel products from the European Union until the year 2002 from the originally planned 1997, PAP news agency said.
PAP quoted deputy industry minister Stanislaw Padykula as saying after a meeting with steel-industry representatives that he would present the proposal to the prime minister.
The industry would use the extra time to complete its restructuring, began in 1992, which will cost an estimated $4 billion, PAP said.
The current import duty on steel is nine percent and will be reduced to three percent next year.

PAP said Padykula was likely to ask the European Union to prolong the period for abolishing Polish duties on steel during November talks with the EU commission on the terms of Poland's future EU membership.

Poland currently has 25 steelworks employing 100,000 workers. Under the restructuring programme, the workforce would be halved and the works would install continuous steel-smelting lines to reduce costs.
